actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

device.name: Lucky Robots G1 pick-and-place scene (MuJoCo model)

facts.text: The scene is a MuJoCo scene named g1_table_red_block with the G1 robot, a ground plane, a brown table, a target table, a red cylindrical block on a free joint, and head, wrist and fixed cameras
The robot model is g1_29dof_rev_1_0, which compiles angles in radians, resolves meshes from assets and uses autolimits
The model integrates with the implicitfast scheme at a 0.005 s timestep, with a pyramidal cone and gravity 0 0 -9.81
The upstream runner also sets model.opt.timestep to 0.005, which it says must match training
The robot base body pelvis is at -0.6 0 0.79 and carries the freejoint floating_base_joint
The G1 has 29 actuated body degrees of freedom: 12 leg, 3 waist and 14 arm joints
The position actuator default class g1 sets inheritrange 1, so an actuator of that class takes its control range from the matching joint range
The joint ranges are explicit, for example the left hip pitch joint is -2.5307 to 2.8798 rad
The actuator section has 29 position actuators of class g1 for the body joints and then 14 position actuators for the finger joints
The 14 finger actuators have a joint but no class, ctrlrange or inheritrange
The right finger joints have explicit ranges: thumb 0 is -1.0472 to 1.0472, thumb 1 -1.0472 to 0.724312, index 0 0 to 1.5708 and index 1 0 to 1.74533
The red block is a free body at 0.0 0.026 0.85 with the freejoint red_block_joint and a cylinder of radius 0.02 and half-height 0.035
The source table top is a 0.8 by 0.5 m box at z 0.713 and the target table top is a 0.7 by 0.5 m box at z 0.613
The head camera head_cam is on the torso
The wrist camera wrist_cam is on the right palm
The upstream runner loads scene.xml, sets the 0.005 s timestep and initializes qpos x -0.6, z 0.76 and the default joint positions before stepping with mj_step
The upstream runner writes the 29 body actuator targets and the right finger targets into data.ctrl, closing the grip to 0.8, -0.9, -1.5, 1.4, 1.5, 1.4 and 1.5 and opening it to 0.0

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates the fixed model deterministically from the model defaults; the bridge accepts a seed in cap.world.reset.v1 but does not use it and a reset restores the model defaults, so one ctrl sequence repeats a trajectory on the same engine.  This package's fake is deterministic too, but its placeholder motion is not the engine's physics.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it parses the scene and its g1.xml include for the two free joints, the 43 hinge joints, the 43 position actuators, the 29 inherited control ranges (the 14 finger actuators have none) and the 0.005 s option step, then moves each actuated joint a placeholder fraction of the remaining distance to its control target; it computes no inertia, torque, contact, friction, gravity, equality, damping, armature or actuator-force dynamics and produces no MuJoCo trajectory

the 14 finger actuators have no ctrlrange in the MJCF (g1.xml:435-449), so the bridge publishes action.ctrl[29] to [42] operator_required: a step that sets them is refused until the site's site-limits.json bounds them; the example overlay's finger joint ranges (g1.xml:254-289,347-382) are operator data, not bounds the model states

the stand-in loads no mesh or texture and resolves no collision or contact, so the red cylinder's free joint is carried in qpos/qvel but the cylinder never falls, rolls or is grasped; the two tables, the ground and the robot links do not collide

the stand-in applies no joint limit, no actuator force range, no sensor or camera model and no implicitfast integration; it carries 57 qpos and 55 qvel values (two free joints and 43 hinge joints) and 43 control values

the bridge reset restores the MJCF model defaults (pelvis at -0.6 0 0.79 with zero joint angles), while run.py resets to a custom pose (x -0.6, z 0.76 and the default joint positions from model_config.json, run.py:637-645); the driver uses mj_resetData, not the runner's pose

NOT COVERED: the RGB camera images of head_cam, wrist_cam, overhead, side_view and tracking, and the ONNX walker, croucher, rotator and right-reacher policies, the keyboard controller, the grip toggle and the model_config.json action scales; cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1 carry the world state and the actuator targets only
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine and the sim backend (real mujoco) was not run
no physical G1 is modelled and nothing was validated against hardware
